A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SynBrain, with matching core methods and alignable main-text and appendix material. Their text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original NSD experiments on fMRI synthesis, subject adaptation, decoding augmentation, architectural ablations and brain activation patterns.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional encoder comparisons, baseline evaluations, subject-adaptation results and augmentation experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 and its accompanying description revise the encoder's initial convolution from kernel 7/padding 3 to kernel 1/padding 0 (v1 Appendix D.1; v3 C.1). The overall BrainVAE/S2N architecture, objectives and inference procedure remain unchanged. This reported architectural revision does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates NSD subjects 1, 2, 5 and 7. v3 adds one-hour adaptation to subjects 3, 4, 6 and 8, extending evaluation to previously excluded participants who completed fewer sessions (Appendix H.2, Table 11). The dataset and synthesis/decoding tasks remain the same.

E2.justification: v3 substantially broadens encoding comparisons by adding GNet and LinearReg for subject-specific synthesis (Table 8), and LinearReg for adaptation from Subject 1 to Subjects 2, 5 and 7 (Table 9). The latter supplies a comparator where v1 reported only SynBrain adaptation results. Existing MindSimulator and decoding comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Additional experiments introduce MAE/DINOv2 encoder configurations, a LinearReg adaptation protocol that freezes its first layer, and synthetic augmentation budgets of 8, 16 and 32 hours beyond the existing 1–4-hour settings. Established main-experiment splits, metrics and training protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F/Table 7 adds a focused encoder-choice ablation using MAE and DINOv2. Appendix H.3/Table 13 extends augmentation sensitivity testing to larger synthetic-data amounts. The existing component, latent-dimensionality, mapper-depth, diffusion-comparison and stochastic-sampling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions average retrieval over 30 sampled sets of 300 candidates and retain the same trial-averaging practice. v3 introduces no training-seed reporting, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Retained table values are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results for encoders, baselines, additional subjects and augmentation budgets. Table 8 reports MSE 0.102 for LinearReg, 0.092 for GNet and 0.079 for SynBrain. Table 13 reports brain retrieval of 61.9% with 32-hour augmentation versus 82.0% with one hour. These are additional conditions, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The reconstruction, KL, contrastive and mapper objectives remain mathematically unchanged, as does the optional additive Gaussian sampling formulation in v1 Appendix F/v3 Appendix E. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: probabilistic neural-response modeling, strong synthesis performance, few-shot adaptation, useful synthetic augmentation and functional consistency. The added experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v3 attributes CLIP's advantage to vision-language supervision, explains practical obstacles to using MindSimulator for cross-subject comparison, and suggests that excessive synthetic augmentation can introduce distributional mismatch or redundancy. The original limitations concerning visual-model biases and unmodeled neural variability remain.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the promised code release with a stated repository address, adds single-A100 feasibility information for the already evaluated d=1024 variant, and specifies additional convolution parameters in Algorithm 2. Appendix G also documents LinearReg's 4096-dimensional hidden layer and adaptation procedure.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for MAE, DINOv2, GNet and AdaBrain-Bench. Section 2.2 also distinguishes MindEye's diffusion prior from MindSimulator's diffusion transformer. The broader positioning against deterministic encoding and existing few-shot decoding methods is retained.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Appendix A to main Section 5, with corresponding section and appendix renumbering. Supplementary sections are expanded, while most existing prose remains intact. Other edits include terminology corrections, local wording refinements and updated author/venue footnotes.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands quantitative displays with dedicated encoder, baseline and augmentation-budget tables (Tables 7–9 and 13), and an additional-subject block in Table 11. Existing figures retain their visual content, while several displays move, including the reversed order of Figure 4 and Table 1.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added regression/GNet comparisons, encoder controls and previously excluded subjects strengthen empirical validation. The larger augmentation sweep clarifies diminishing returns, and the repository address improves reproducibility information. These are useful, bounded gains over an otherwise stable paper. They outweigh a new overstatement in Appendix G: retrieval superiority over LinearReg is claimed even though its retrieval scores are not reported.
